 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 09.04.2010 at about 11.00 a.m., the deceased - Ravikumar was proceeding in a motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-13/Q-8181 along with one pillion rider from Devegowda Nagar to Hassan and when he reached near Bittagodanahalli, a car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MD-5619 came from Sakaleshpur side in a rash and negligent NC: 2023:KHC:24891 manner and dashed against the motorbike.
Due to the impact the deceased - Ravikumar succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the legal heirs of deceased - Ravikumar have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.

The Tribunal has granted the compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl.
No . Particulars

Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Loss of dependency 5,76,000.00 2. Loss of love and affection 10,000.00 3. Loss of estate 10,000.00 4. Loss of consortium 10,000.00 5.
Funeral expenses 10,000.00 Total 6,16,000.00 5.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.6,16,000/- in total under the head 'loss of dependency' and other heads by holding notional income of Rs.4,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC:24891 p.m.
It is stated that the deceased was doing agricultural work and business man and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- p.m.
But there is no proof of income.
The accident is of the year 2010.
In the absence of any proof of income, a sum of Rs.5,500/- p.m., is to be taken into consideration as notional income as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The deceased was aged 35 years.
Considering the age of the deceased, 40% of the income is to be added towards 'loss of future prospects in life' and 1/4th is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
As the deceased was aged 35 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.

Therefore,

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.7,01,800/- (Rs.13,17,800 - Rs.6,16,000) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the NC: 2023:KHC:24891 date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.2004/2010 dated 07.09.2011, is hereby modified holding the claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,01,800/- with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 223 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.
